newsitem.title: USA: TALKING POINT - HFS PHH a powerhouse link.
newsitem.headline: TALKING POINT - HFS PHH a powerhouse link.

text.p: Continuing its dizzying wave of acquisitions, HFS Inc went shopping again on Monday, this time striking a $1.7 billion deal to buy PHH Corp to bring together two firms with highly complementary real estate and automotive operations.

Despite HFS's offer to pay a 60 percent premium over PHH's closing share price Friday, analysts had widespread praise for the deal, which pairs businesses and customer bases that appear to be far stronger together than apart.
In one key way, analysts said, the deal is unlike many others, particularly stock deals that can require a year or more of integration before earnings per share growth resumes.

"This deal is immediately accretive to earnings," said Michael Mueller, analyst at Montgomery Securities. Mueller, who raised his 1997 earnings estimate on HFS to $2.55 per share from $2.20 on news of the deal, added, "It's a case where being part of HFS strengthens PHH and vice versa."
Mark Manson, an analyst at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette, agreed. Manson who rates HFS a buy, raised his 12-month price target on the shares to 100 from 90 based on the acquisition.
"It's a terrific deal, really, from the perspective of both parties," said Manson. "There just seem to be a lot of ways these companies augment each other."

Among the links analysts cited are those between PHH's auto fleet management operation, which purchases cars for corporate leasing, and auto rental giant Avis Inc, which HFS acquired for $800 million just a month ago.
"HFS continues to make smart acqusitions," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "This fits with their most recent acquisition of Avis."

At first, HFS and PHH will likely benefit on the purchasing side of the auto business, said analysts. "PHH buys 100,000 cars a year," noted Manson, ticking off volume purchase discounts as the most immediate possible synergies.
Another potential benefit is in the disparate customer bases of the two companies. PHH largely relies on corporate and government contracts, analysts said, while HFS tends to serve individuals.

Still, the most powerful of the integration opportunities may lie in the combination of PHH's relocation and mortgage origination businesses with HFS's vast army of real estate brokerages, which include Coldwell Banker, acquired in May for $740 million, and Century 21 acquired last August.

HFS also owns real estate franchiser Electronic Realty Associates (ERA), purchased within the last year, and has a $625 million-plus acquisition of Indiana-based Resort Condominiums International Inc pending, with closing due by the end of the year.

"PHH's relocation business is a very significant addition because that's how a lot of real estate brokers get leads," said Montgomery analyst Mueller. "Right now, PHH works primarily with brokers that are not affiliated with HFS."
In turn, HFS's real estate brokers offer a deep well of business for PHH's mortgage origination operation, which is now the 12th largest in the U.S.

Analysts also cited a subtle financial benefit to the combination, under which HFS will issue 23.2 million shares for the 34.8 million PHH shares outstanding. PHH, they noted, has a better credit rating than its acquirer.

While none of the debt rating agencies had yet weighed in with their opinions, equity analysts said the purchase could lead to a reduction in HFS's cost of capital because of the improvement to its credit profile.
